questions.question: Brihadisvara Temple is located in _______.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: 'Thanjavur' (Option 3).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadisvara Temple**

 
 
• Also known as the Rajarajeswaram or Peruvudaiyar Kovil, it is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• It is located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• The temple was built by Raja Raja Chola I between 1003 and 1010 AD.
 
• It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site known as the "Great Living Chola Temples".
 
• The temple is renowned for its architecture, massive size, and the stunning sculptures that adorn its walls.
 
• It features a massive lingam (symbol of Shiva) and is one of the largest temples in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Other Options__**

__
 
• **Hampi**

 
 
• Hampi is a historic village located in Karnataka, India.
 
• It was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century.
 
• It is known for its ruins, temples, and monuments spread across a vast area, including the famous Virupaksha Temple.
 
 
 
• **Kanchipuram**
 
 
• Kanchipuram, also known as Kanchi, is a city in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is known as the "City of a Thousand Temples" and is famous for its historical temples and silk sarees.
 
• Notable temples include the Ekambareswarar Temple and the Kailasanathar Temple.
 
 
 
• **Sarnath**
 
 
• Sarnath is a place located near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It is an important Buddhist site where Gautama Buddha first taught the Dharma after his enlightenment.
 
• Key attractions include the Dhamek Stupa and the Ashoka Pillar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chola Dynasty:**__

 __
 
• The Chola dynasty was a Tamil dynasty that ruled primarily in southern India until the 13th century.
 
• They are renowned for their contributions to art, architecture, and culture, especially temple architecture.
 
• The Brihadisvara Temple is a prime example of Chola architectural brilliance and their devotion to Shaivism.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**__
 
 
• Sites listed by UNESCO for their cultural, historical, or scientific significance.
 
• The "Great Living Chola Temples" include the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, the Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.
 
• These temples are celebrated for their grand architecture, intricate sculptures, and historical importance.

questions.question:
**Match the following styles of temple architecture in India with their respective characteristics:**

 
 

 Column A
 Column B
 
 

 1. Nagara Style 
 a) Vimana tower with multiple tiers and gopuram
 
 

 2. Dravida Style 
 b) Curvilinear shikhara with amalaka at the top
 
 

 3. Vesara Style 
 c) Deula with a prominent Rekha Deula (tower) over sanctum
 
 

 4. Kalinga Style 
 d) Hybrid style with features of both Nagara and Dravida
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: '1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **1. Nagara Style - Curvilinear shikhara with amalaka at the top (b)**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Nagara style of architecture features a curvilinear shikhara (spire) that typically has an amalaka (a stone disc) at the top, which is characteristic of Northern Indian temples.
 
 
 
• **2. Dravida Style - Vimana tower with multiple tiers and gopuram (a)**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Dravida style, predominant in Southern India, is characterized by a vimana (tower) with multiple tiers and elaborate entrance gateways known as gopurams.
 
 
 
• **3. Vesara Style - Hybrid style with features of both Nagara and Dravida (d)**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Vesara style is a combination of the Nagara and Dravida styles, featuring characteristics from both architectural traditions.
 
 
 
• **4. Kalinga Style - Deula with a prominent Rekha Deula (tower) over sanctum (c)**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The Kalinga style is known for its distinctive deula (temple) architecture, which features a prominent Rekha Deula (tower) over the sanctum, typically found in Odisha.
 
 

**Hence, the correct matches are: 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Styles of Temple Architecture in India:**__

 
 
• **Nagara Style:** Predominantly found in Northern India, characterized by its tall, curvilinear shikhara and intricate carvings.
 
• **Dravida Style:** Found in Southern India, noted for its gopurams and multi-tiered vimanas, typically adorned with sculptures and carvings.
 
• **Vesara Style:** A blend of Nagara and Dravida styles, incorporating elements of both in its design, often seen in temples of Karnataka.
 
• **Kalinga Style:** Specific to Odisha, featuring deulas with a distinct Rekha Deula and elaborate sculptural decorations.

questions.question: With reference to the Qutub Minar, Which of the following statement is correct?

options.text: It is named after the famous Sufi Khwaja Qutubuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
Construction of the first balcony of this building was done by Qutubuddin Aibak around 1299.
Qutb Minar was repaired by Alauddin Khalji only.
Qutub Minar's surrounding contains the Lahori Darwaza(Gate).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Qutub Minar**

 
• **Qutbuddin Aibak constructed Qutb Minar in 1199. **
 
• **It is a five-storey building, named after the famous Sufi Khwaja Qutubuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Construction of the first balcony of this building was done by Qutubuddin Aibak around 1199 and the remaining floors were constructed by Iltutmish. ***Hence, Statement 2 is not correct.*
 
• **It was repaired by Alauddin Khalji, Muhammed Tughluq, Firuz Shah Tughluq and Ibrahim Lodi. ***Hence, Statement 3 is not correct.*
 
• The pattern is created under the **balcony **by the small arches and geometrical designs.
 
• The surface of the minar is curved and angular.
 
• It is built by Muslim conquerors in the thirteenth century to commemorate their** final triumph over the Rajput rulers of Delh**i (Qutub means victory).
 
• It also served as a **tower from where muezzins (criers) call for prayer** at the Quwwatu’l-Islam mosque nearby.
 
• A 7 m-high iron pillar stands in the courtyard of the mosque.
 
• **Its surrounding contains the Alai-Darwaza Gate,** the masterpiece of Indo-Muslim art (built in 1311).** ***Hence, Statement 4 is not correct.*
 
• The building process of Qutub Minar took about 75 years.
 
• The minar (tower) is engraved with **fine arabesque decorations** on its surface, mainly verses from the Quran.
 
• Qutub Minar and its monuments were declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.**

questions.question: Dilwara Temples at Mount Abu, Rajasthan is an example of _____ temple architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jain.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dilwara Temples** is a group of five **Jain temples** located in **Mount Abu, Rajasthan.**
 
• The temples were built between the **11th and 13th centuries AD** and are considered to be one of the finest examples of **Jain temple architecture.**
 
• The temples are known for their** intricate marble carvings and exquisite craftsmanship.**
 
• The temples are dedicated to different** Jain Tirthankaras** and are named after them.
 
• The temples are a popular tourist destination and attract visitors from all over the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhist temple architecture** is characterized by the use of wood and stone and features intricate carvings and paintings. However, Dilwara Temples are not Buddhist temples.
 
• **Mughal architecture** is a blend of Indian, Persian, and Islamic styles and is known for its use of red sandstone and marble. However, Dilwara Temples do not follow the Mughal style of architecture.
 
• **Dravida temple architecture** is a style of temple architecture that originated in the southern part of India and is characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers and intricate carvings. However, Dilwara Temples do not follow the Dravida style of architecture.

questions.question: The famous painting "Dying Princess" is in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ajanta Caves__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dying Princess:

 
 
• The 'Dying Princess' is inscribed in Cave No. 16 of Ajanta Caves.
 
• The cave is one of the oldest in the world, first revealing the Hinayana period (200 BCE to 200 BCE), where Buddha is represented only by symbols, or in his supposed previous existence as related in the Jataka stories.
 
• The scene shows the critical stage of Nanda’s wife.
 
• Nanda is a cousin and brother of Buddha.
 
• She fell ill after hearing the decision of her husband to renounce the crown and become a monk.
 
• It is a depiction of poetic tragedy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ajanta Caves:

 
 
• The Ajanta Caves are approximately 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments.
 
• They can be dated from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra.
 
• They are universally regarded as masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.
 
• The Ajanta Caves were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68719d242e8dd0ad27727e05f6226d1cda3a15032a01a771f5bbbb323f54c68e.png] 

 
• Dying Princess of Ajanta Cave

questions.question: Rambhar Stupa is a popular tourist destination for Buddhists located in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kushinagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Ramabhar Stupa is a Buddhist monument in **Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is situated near Buddha Ghat and is one of the most important pilgrim places for Buddhists in India.
 
• Ramabhar Stupa holds a great religious significance to Buddhists all over the world as it is said that this is the exact spot where Lord Buddha was cremated and got Mahaparinirvana after his death in 483 BC.
 
• The stupa was constructed by the Malla Kings who ruled over Kushinagar when Buddha was alive.
 
• In ancient Buddhist texts, this Stupa has been referred to as Mukut-Bandhan Chaitya or Mukta-Bandhan Vihara.

questions.question: Where is the famous Meenakshi Amman temple located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madurai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Meenakshi Amman Temple is located on the Southern Bank of the Vaigai River in the temple city of Madurai, in Tamil Nadu. 

 
 
• This temple dedicated to Thirukamakottam Udaya Aaludaiya Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort, Sundareshwar, a form of Shiva.
 
• In this temple, both God and Goddess are worshipped together in separate chambers.
 
• The temple is at the **centre of the ancient temple city Madurai.**
 
• It was built by King Kulasekara Pandya.
 
• It is a complex made in accordance with the Shilpa Shastra and has 5 main entrances with **14 gateway towers or 'gopurams',** **golden 'Vimanas', holy sanctums and shrines dedicated to the revered Goddess Meenakshi and many others. **

questions.question: Which fort is known as Gibraltar of Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taragarh Fort**__.

__
 
• **Taragarh Fort **is known as** Gibraltar of Rajasthan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gibraltar **is the location where one can look after in all directions from one place.
 
• **Taragarh fort **of **Ajmer **is called **Gibraltar of Rajasthan**.
 
• With the help of this fort, the protection of the whole city can be assured as one can view the whole city from all sides of the fort.
 
• The fort of **Taragarh **is a wonderful example of invasion, security, and architecture.
 
• It is famous for its glorious history.
 
• This fort is located on the **highest mountain range** of the **Ajmer**.
 
• It was seen by the** Governor-General of India, William Bentick** in **1832 **and said, "**Oh, the** **second Gibraltor of the world**".
 
• The Mughal Emperor Akbar realized its importance and make Ajmer the largest province of his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38ee197a622ef7cea0a2c2d4d972766a99fdf4ba043909b24a1c01eccfb2a96d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Amber Fort**
 
 
 
• Amer Fort is a fort located in Amber, Rajasthan.
 
• Raja Man Singh I began construction in 1592 and the palace, which was built as a strong, safe haven against attacking enemies, was completed by Mirja Raja Jai Singh.
 
 
 
 

 **Kumbhalgarh Fort**
 
 
 
• Architect of Kumbhalgarh Fort Rajasthan named Manda.
 
• It is perfectly perched between eleven peaks of the Aravalli ranges.
 
 
 
 

 **Chittorgarh Fort**
 
 
 
• This fort is one of the largest forts in India.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The fort was the capital of Mewar and is located in the present-day town of Chittorgarh.
